title: Momentum Contrastive Learning (MoCo)
reading: The slide presents MoCo as a contrastive objective that maximizes similarity of positive pairs and minimizes similarity of negative pairs. A schematic below shows the two-encoder architecture with a similarity matrix loss, plus the momentum update rule for the key encoder.

visuals.description: Key image feeds a purple 'Encoder' (encoder k) and query image feeds a green 'Encoder' (encoder q); both outputs form a similarity matrix (grid with highlighted diagonal cells) labelled 'loss'. A red arrow shows gradients updating encoder q only, while text and equation θ_k := m θ_k + (1−m) θ_q indicate encoder k is updated by a moving average.
visuals.assertion: Only the query encoder is trained by gradients from the contrastive loss; the key encoder's parameters track it via a momentum (exponential moving average) update, and the diagonal of the similarity matrix are the positive pairs.

concepts.name: MoCo (Momentum Contrast)
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised representation learning with a slowly-updated key encoder for consistent negatives.

concepts.name: Momentum/moving-average parameter update
concepts.why_it_matters: Keeps key representations consistent across batches.

verbatim_spans: Update encoder k by moving average
